finding: Opioids were detected in 3.5% of samples expected to be methamphetamine. Across 8,889 samples not expected to contain an opioid, 189 (2%) contained one, most of them (61.4%) at trace concentration (below 0.50% wt/wt).
where_when: Substance Drug Checking, British Columbia, Canada; samples collected 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2023 (published 2025)
source: Wallace B, Shkolnikov I, Kielty C, et al. Is fentanyl in everything? Examining the unexpected occurrence of illicit opioids in British Columbia's drug supply. Harm Reduction Journal 2025;22:28. doi:10.1186/s12954-025-01189-w

finding: Samples sold as methamphetamine (and as MDMA or heroin) were consistently found to contain only the advertised substance, in a set of 103 samples bought from cryptomarkets; the abstract does not give the number of methamphetamine samples.
where_when: Australia (samples bought from cryptomarkets), tested by the Vancouver-based Get Your Drugs Tested service; Test4Pay forum data from 1 September 2022 to 23 August 2023 (published 2024)
source: Barratt MJ, Ball M, Wong GTW, Quinton A. Adulteration and substitution of drugs purchased in Australia from cryptomarkets: An analysis of Test4Pay. Drug and Alcohol Review 2024;43(4):969–974. doi:10.1111/dar.13825

finding: Substitution: among the 33 samples sold as MDMA, 3 of those that contained no MDMA contained methamphetamine ('crystal Meth').
where_when: Electronic music festival near Mexico City, Mexico; published 2023 (festival date not captured in this session)
source: Cruz SL, Bencomo-Cruz M, Medina-Mora ME, et al. First drug-checking study at an electronic festival and fentanyl detection in the central region of Mexico. Harm Reduction Journal 2023;20:174. doi:10.1186/s12954-023-00905-8
